pages.title: What wears LP blades
text: An LP turbine's rotor is two blade sections, A and B, one per flow. Each wears from 0 to 100 %. The BLADES tab of the turbine screen shows them.

Wet steam erodes them, as before. Closing the generator breaker out of phase twists the shaft: about 4 times rated torque at 90 degrees, 5 at 120. Over 110 % speed the blades stretch, and at 150 % a disc bursts. Nothing trips the turbine for you.

pages.title: Reverse power
text: A generator left on the grid with too little steam is driven by the grid as a motor. The screen shows reverse power in MW.

With no steam doing the work, windage heats the LP's last stages. The exhaust hood passes 120 C in about a minute and a half, and the blades fail after about nine minutes. Open the breaker yourself: nothing does it for you.

pages.title: Turbine missiles
text: A failed blade section on a shaft over half speed throws a blade: 45 kg at about 400 m/s, nearly 4 MJ. It flies across the shaft in the plane of the wheel and breaks through blocks while its energy lasts, about four of stone. A burst disc throws far more.
It stops in unbreakable blocks, another machine casing, or a chunk that is not loaded. The section is wrecked and the whole train shakes until you stop it.

pages.title: The turbine hall crane
text: The building crane works over turbines too: the same runway rails, console and pendant, no reactor needed. Put rails at least 12 blocks above the turbine floor.
Add a Casing Laydown Stand with 7 x 7 of clear floor, and an LP Blade Storage Stand. Both must lie between the rails. The pendant gains COVER OFF / ON and BLADES OUT / IN.

pages.title: Changing a blade section
text: Close the valves, open the breaker and let the shaft stop. Roll it cold on the turning gear, then switch the gear off. The casing must be under 100 C with no steam in it.
COVER OFF puts the 110 t hood on its stand. BLADES OUT lifts the worse 62 t section onto a saddle. BLADES IN sets a spare in, as new. COVER ON closes it. Steam into an open casing just vents.

pages.title: Blade sections and stands
text: Craft an LP Turbine Blade Section from four iron blocks, four iron ingots and a diamond (steel with Mekanism). A section over 5 % worn comes out of a turbine as a Damaged LP Blade Section; craft that alone to scrap it for iron.
The blade stand holds two sections. Hoppers and pipes can stock or empty it, and you can right-click one on or sneak-click one off. Breaking a stand drops what it holds.

pages.title: Wrecked casings
text: A thrown blade tears a hole in the casing where it leaves; the LP still runs. A burst disc bursts the casing open: it holds no steam, whatever the valves admit vents into the hall, until it is rebuilt.
The BLADES tab shows the Casing: sound, holed, BURST or SHAFT OUT.

pages.title: The shaft excursion
text: The worst case. A rotor whose disc burst is a third of a disc out of balance. Drive it on to 180 % speed and the coupling shears: one rotor half, 62 t, breaks out of the casing and rolls across the floor, breaking what is in its way.
It comes to rest as a Turbine Shaft Wreck. The rest of the train is wrecked and grinds to a stop.

pages.title: Oil filter
text: A pumped Main Oil Tank loses about 0.9 L/s of oil: a 1,000 L drum lasts 18 minutes. Bolt an Oil Filter Housing straight against the tank and put an Oil Filter Cartridge in its slot, and the tank loses a tenth of that: a drum lasts three hours.

The cartridge loads up with use, faster with hot oil, and lasts about six hours. At 12 psid across it a change is due; when it is full, or the slot is empty, the oil goes round it and is lost at the old rate. Taking a cartridge out gives back a used one; nothing cleans it.

pages.title: Turbine fires
text: A bearing run without oil at speed passes 300 C in about a minute and lights the oil in its housing. A disc fragment, a blade thrown down through the oil lines or the rotor half cuts a line: 1,000 L catches. An excursion lets the generator's hydrogen out to burn.
Running oil pumps feed an oil fire. Water on the fire puts it out. A burning section loses 0.4 % a second.

pages.title: Rebuilding a wreck
text: Stop the shaft, put out the fire, COVER OFF (a wrecked hood comes off) and lift both blade sections out. Use a Turbine Rebuild Kit on the empty casing: new bearings, couplings and glands. Then two spares in and a new hood on.
An HP or generator takes a kit by hand. The crane lifts a shaft wreck with BLADES OUT, or break it with a pickaxe.
